name: Abraham
charge: Obeying the Lord's voice; keeping his charge, his commandments, his statutes, and his laws
summary: Told to leave country, kindred and father's house for a land he would be shewed, he went. Told to offer his only son, he rose early in the morning. The Lord's own account of him, given to Isaac, is the law kept: Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.
offense: Three great tests display a faith that acts upon the command. He left country, kindred and father's house for a destination he was not told (Genesis 12:1). He circumcised every male of his house on the day he was commanded (Genesis 17:23), at ninety-nine years old, receiving in his flesh the token of the covenant God had explained to him (Genesis 17:10-14; Genesis 17:24). And when the son through whom the whole promise ran was demanded, he rose early in the morning (Genesis 22:3), which is the detail the record chooses to report. Genesis 18 adds that he was expected to command his household after him to keep the way of the Lord (Genesis 18:19) and to do justice and judgment, and the Lord's own summary in Genesis 26 states the standard he met (Genesis 26:5): he kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws. He believed the Lord, and it was counted to him for righteousness (Genesis 15:6). That faith did not end in agreement with a promise. Hebrews explains that, when Isaac was required, Abraham accounted God able to raise him even from the dead (Hebrews 11:17-19). The angel stopped his hand, and he offered the ram provided in his son's stead (Genesis 22:11-13). James joins the offering to the earlier faith: faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect (James 2:21-23).
judgment: The promise was enlarged at each stage and finally sworn. After Moriah God swore by himself, having no greater to swear by, that the seed would be multiplied and that in it all the nations of the earth would be blessed (Genesis 22:15-18), and the ground given is explicit: because thou hast obeyed my voice (Genesis 22:18). He was called the friend of God, and the land covenant was made with his seed (Genesis 15:18; Isaiah 41:8). The promise continued through Isaac and Jacob, and the inheritance was divided among the twelve tribes (Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 44:19-22).

verses.text: Now the Lord had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto a land that I will shew thee:
And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing:
And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.
So Abram departed, as the Lord had spoken unto him; and Lot went with him: and Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran.
And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.
And he believed in the Lord; and he counted it to him for righteousness.

And Abraham took Ishmael his son, and all that were born in his house, and all that were bought with his money, every male among the men of Abraham’s house; and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin in the selfsame day, as God had said unto him.
And Abraham was ninety years old and nine, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
And Ishmael his son was thirteen years old, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
In the selfsame day was Abraham circumcised, and Ishmael his son.
And all the men of his house, born in the house, and bought with money of the stranger, were circumcised with him.
And the Lord said, Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do;
Seeing that Abraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him?

For I know him, that he will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment; that the Lord may bring upon Abraham that which he hath spoken of him.
And it came to pass after these things, that God did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, here I am.

And he said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of.

And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and saddled his ass, and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son, and clave the wood for the burnt offering, and rose up, and went unto the place of which God had told him.
And the angel of the Lord called unto Abraham out of heaven the second time,
And said, By myself have I sworn, saith the Lord, for because thou hast done this thing, and hast not withheld thy son, thine only son:

That in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand which is upon the sea shore; and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies;
And in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed; because thou hast obeyed my voice.

Sojourn in this land, and I will be with thee, and will bless thee; for unto thee, and unto thy seed, I will give all these countries, and I will perform the oath which I sware unto Abraham thy father;
And I will make thy seed to multiply as the stars of heaven, and will give unto thy seed all these countries; and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed;
Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.
By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.
By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:
For he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.
By faith Abraham, when he was tried, offered up Isaac: and he that had received the promises offered up his only begotten son,
Of whom it was said, That in Isaac shall thy seed be called:
Accounting that God was able to raise him up, even from the dead; from whence also he received him in a figure.
Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he had offered Isaac his son upon the altar?
Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?
And the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.

entries.commentary: The Most High called Abram to get out of his country, from his kindred, and from his father's house. He called Abraham alone, and blessed him, and increased him. Some hold back from repenting because of what family or friends may say. Do not let your kindred hold you back from being blessed and increased; when the Most High calls you out, you have to go. Confessing Christ before men means something. When Christ asked, Whom say ye that I am, Peter confessed, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God; whoever confesses Him before men, He confesses before His Father, and He came to set a man at variance against his own household for the truth's sake.

In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed is not talking about everybody. The children of the prophets and of the covenant are Israel, and Israel would be scattered into all nations of the earth; through Abraham's seed the kindreds of the earth are blessed because scattered Israel gets the chance to repent and return, circumcised or not.
Abram departed at seventy and five years old, with Sarai and Lot, into the land of Canaan; Canaan is northeast Africa.
Sarai was around the same age as Abram, about ten years apart, and she was still a very fair woman to look upon in her sixties.

The Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, and Pharaoh sent Abram away with his wife and all that he had. The Most High protected the household of Abram in Egypt. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

Abram asked what the Lord would give him, seeing he went childless and the steward of his house, Eliezer of Damascus, stood to inherit everything. The word came: This shall not be thine heir; he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir. The Most High prophesied children to Abram out of his own seed.

Look now toward heaven and tell the stars: so shall thy seed be. Abram believed the Lord, and it was counted to him for righteousness. Righteousness is immortal, and righteousness is defined by the law: it shall be our righteousness if we observe to do all these commandments. Abram's faith showed itself in his works.

Abram divided the heifer, the goat, and the ram, and drove the fowls from the carcases; he was offering sacrifice. When the sun went down a deep sleep and a horror of great darkness fell on Abram: he was about to receive a vision of future prophecy. The Most High speaks in a dream, in a vision of the night, and reveals His secret to His servants the prophets.

Know of a surety: thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, shall serve them, and be afflicted four hundred years. This prophecy was fulfilled in Egypt; the sojourning of the children of Israel in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years, and the four hundred was an approximation of that time. This verse is not the doctrine about America and 1619. The northern kingdom's captivity on this side began in 1492, and by that counting the years pass four hundred and Israel is still in captivity and still scattered this day; the prophecy of [Genesis 15:13](/bible/genesis/15#v13) was fulfilled at the Exodus. They came out with great substance: the children of Israel required jewels of silver and gold and raiment of the Egyptians, and they spoiled Egypt as they left. The twelve tribes scattered among the nations today, the people called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans, are the seed this covenant history belongs to. Abram himself would go to his fathers in peace and be buried in a good old age; and the seed would return in the fourth generation, for the iniquity of the Amorites was not yet full.

At ninety and nine years old Abram was commanded to walk before the Most High and be perfect. There is no age excuse; Christ said nothing new in [Matthew 5:48](/bible/matthew/5#v48), for the command to be perfect was given thousands of years before. Perfect according to the scriptures means to walk in His statutes and keep His commandments; that is how Israel perfects itself.

When the Most High began dealing with Abram on a covenant level, his name was changed: Abram became Abraham, a father of many nations, and kings would come out of him. Father of many nations does not mean everybody is spiritually a child of Abraham. The same promise was passed down the seed line: Jacob's name was changed to Israel and told a nation and a company of nations and kings would come out of his loins. The blessing of all men and the covenant were made to rest upon the head of Jacob and divided among the twelve tribes. Kings come out of that seed, including Christ, the King of kings.
The covenant is with Abraham's seed after him, and seed is literal offspring, not a spiritual metaphor. The Most High promised to be a God to Abraham and to his seed after him.

Circumcision is the token of the covenant: every man child circumcised at eight days, and the uncircumcised soul cut off from his people. Abraham received circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of the faith he had yet being uncircumcised. He believed and obeyed first, and circumcision sealed it; likewise a brother can come into the truth, get built up in the faith, and then go through with the process. It still has to be done. A covenant is a contract with terms; the covenant was confirmed to Jacob for a law, and circumcision is one of the laws within the covenant.

Sarai's name was changed to Sarah, and she shall be a mother of nations; those are the same nations of the covenant, and she and Abraham had one child together, Isaac. Abraham fell on his face and laughed in his heart: shall a child be born to a hundred year old man, and Sarah bear at ninety? The Most High read his thought and named the child from it: Isaac means he will laugh.

Ishmael received a blessing: fruitful, multiplied exceedingly, twelve princes, a great nation. But the word to Abraham was kings shall come out of thee, and the covenant passes to Isaac: my covenant will I establish with Isaac. Not all who are of Abraham's seed are the children; in Isaac shall thy seed be called. Ishmael was born of the flesh, of Sarai's plan, with no word from God ordaining it; the children of the promise are counted for the seed.

The selfsame day Abraham circumcised every male of his house, himself at ninety and nine and Ishmael at thirteen. That is the righteous example: he received the commandment and performed it the same day.

The three men who stood by Abraham were angels of the Lord, and they had bodies: their feet were washed with water, they rested under the tree, and they did eat. Be careful how you deal with people, for some have entertained angels unawares. Abraham hastened to serve them. He commanded his household; he told Sarah, Make ready quickly. That is the level of his hospitality and his leadership.

Sarah was barren from the beginning and it had ceased to be with her after the manner of women; she laughed within herself at the promise of a son. The Lord answered the thought she never spoke: Wherefore did Sarah laugh? She denied it out of fear, and He said, Nay, but thou didst laugh. The Most High sees what is within the mind. Is any thing too hard for the Lord? The barren woman is made a joyful mother of children. Through faith Sarah received strength to conceive when she was past age, and Abraham, as good as dead at a hundred, staggered not at the promise but was strong in faith, fully persuaded that what He had promised He was able to perform.

The Lord said, I know Abraham, that he will command his children and his household after him. The man is the leader who makes the rules and keeps his house in the way of the Lord. What makes a great husband and father is commanding the household in the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment. Where men walk away from justice and judgment, they cannot properly command their household.

The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah was great and their sin very grievous. The iniquity of Sodom was pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness; she strengthened not the hand of the poor and needy, was haughty, and committed abomination. The same iniquities fill the land that is spiritually called Sodom today: pride, wealth, idleness from morning to night, and abomination made law.

Abraham drew near and negotiated with the Most High because his nephew Lot dwelt in Sodom; that is why he pleaded for the city. Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right? Abraham reasoned from fifty righteous down to forty and five, forty, thirty, twenty, and ten, and the Lord said, I will not destroy it for ten's sake. Below ten there was no more negotiating, and the Lord went His way.

God did tempt Abraham: Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac. Ishmael was alive, but the Most High counted Isaac the only son, because Ishmael was born of the flesh, of a plan the Lord never spoke, while Isaac was the child of the promise. Abraham rose up early in the morning and went. No hesitation, no debating with the word; that is obedience.
Isaac asked, Where is the lamb for a burnt offering? Abraham answered, My son, God will provide himself a lamb. He trusted the Most High with what was missing.

Abraham bound Isaac, laid him on the altar, and stretched forth his hand with the knife; the angel called out of heaven in the midst of it: Lay not thine hand upon the lad. Now I know that thou fearest God. The fear of God is proved in obedience; they that fear the Lord will not disobey His word. Abraham's inner faith carried him: he accounted that God was able to raise Isaac up, even from the dead, since the promise stood in Isaac who had no children yet. Faith and the commandments go together; you cannot have one without the other.

Once the obedience was fulfilled, God provided the sacrifice: a ram caught in a thicket by his horns, offered in the stead of his son, just as Abraham had told Isaac. Abraham called the place Jehovahjireh: in the mount of the Lord it shall be seen.

By myself have I sworn, saith the Lord: in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven and as the sand upon the sea shore, and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies. The seed possessing the gate of his enemies is part of the covenant: the seed of Jacob shall possess the remnant of Edom and of all the heathen, and Edom shall be a possession. That is why all nations cannot be inside this covenant; the covenant has Israel possessing their enemies. In thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed: those nations are the nations of Israel, the twelve tribes.

In the famine Isaac was told, Go not down into Egypt; the oath sworn to Abraham was performed unto Isaac: seed as the stars, all these countries, and in thy seed shall all nations of the earth be blessed. In thy seed shall all nations be blessed does not put everybody in the covenant. The seed is Christ, and the children of the prophets and of the covenant are Israel, scattered into every nation; through Christ scattered Israel in all kindreds of the earth receives repentance and comes back to the Father. The reason the oath stood: because Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.

Isaac said of Rebekah, She is my sister, fearing the men of the place, and Abimelech saw Isaac sporting with Rebekah his wife and knew. Take the lesson from the sporting: love your wife, play with your wife, keep the flirting and the freshness in the marriage. Give her love, attention, and affection all the days.

Isaac sowed and received in the same year an hundredfold, and the man waxed great until he became very great; and the Philistines envied him and stopped the wells with earth. The nations envy the prosperity of Israel. It is not for anything done to them; the blessing itself is what is hated.
Isaac digged again the wells of his father and the herdmen strove for Esek and Sitnah; he removed and digged Rehoboth, and they strove not: for now the Lord hath made room for us.

Abimelech came saying, We have done unto thee nothing but good, though his people had stopped the wells and sent Isaac away. Isaac answered plainly: Wherefore come ye to me, seeing ye hate me? Isaac was not simple; he separated from the people that hated him rather than assimilating among them, and he dealt with their covenant with open eyes. The words can be like butter while war is in the heart.

Esau at forty took wives of the Hittites, and they were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah. He went straight against the fathers' law of marrying within the kindred; that is the nature of the vessel.
